Vide impugned judgement of conviction dt 30.08.2019 the appellant, an IAS officer of 1986 batch
of Nagaland cadre, was convicted under Section 417 r/w section 415 IPC, under Section 471 IPC r/w
Section 467 IPC and under Section 25 of Arms Act, 1959. Further, vide order of sentence dt 02.09.2019, appellant was sentenced to undergo rigorous
imprisonment of one year for the offense u/s 417 IPC r/w section 415 IPC, rigorous imprisonment of
two years and fine of Rs. 50,000/− for the offense u/s 25 of Arms Act with default in payment of fine
to further undergo simple imprisonment for six months and rigorous imprisonment of five years
with fine of Rs. 1,00,000/− for offense u/s 471 r/w section 467 IPC with default in payment of fine
to further undergo simple imprisonment for one year. Trial Court was pleased to acquit the
accused/appellant in respect of offense u/s 420 and 467 IPC but convicted u/s 417 r/w section 415
IPC with the help of Section 222 of CrPC. Appellant/accused was also convicted by the Ld. Appellant/accused was sentenced
accordingly as noted above. 9315NH/New
dt 24.09.1985 Ex.PW2/C and thus acquitted him of the charge u/s 420 IPC.S. Further perusal of the judgment shows that even though no specific charge was framed against
the appellant but with the help of Section 222 of Cr.P.C, appellant/accused was convicted under
Section 417 IPC r/w section 415 IPC. Trial Court to this effect is hereby set aside and appellant is hereby
acquitted of offense under Section 417 IPC r/w Section 415 IPC and offense under Section 471 IPC
r/w Section 467 IPC. CBI DOJ 10.07.2020 Page No.38 of 57 appellant
qua the offense under Section 25 of the Arms Act is liable to be set aside. Ahluwalia vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 10 July, 2020
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29769628/ 22
and a different order may be passed. In our opinion, a change of
opinion per se on the same materials cannot be a ground for reviewing or reconsidering the earlier
order refusing to grant sanction.
